entity_title: Sponsor the M-Trabajador visa for a local hire
fact_text: A third-country national hired by a Colombian company on an employment contract needs the Migrant (M) visa in the 'Trabajador' category (M category 8). It is granted to foreigners who will work for a legal entity under a contract of employment and is the correct route for a corporate hire; Mercosur and Andean nationals have their own M categories, but an EU or US professional does not qualify for those.
evidence_quote: Para extranjeros que aspiran a trabajar en Colombia con persona jurídica mediante contrato de trabajo.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a generic 'work visa' or a business visa covers a local hire. Actually Colombia requires the specific Migrant (M) 'Trabajador' category, tied to an employment contract with a Colombian legal entity. Action: apply for the M-Trabajador visa before the employee starts work.

entity_title: Never let staff work on a visitor (V) visa
fact_text: The Visitor (V) visa, including V-Negocios (business), is issued only for temporary activity with no intention of establishing domicile in Colombia. A business trip or visa-exempt tourist entry is not work authorization for a local hire; the employee must hold an M-Trabajador visa to be employed and paid in Colombia.
evidence_quote: La Visa de Visitante se expide para aquellas actividades en las que el titular realiza una actividad temporal en el país, sin ánimo de establecer domicilio en el territorio nacional.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a business (V-Negocios) or tourist entry lets someone start while the paperwork catches up. Actually the V visa expressly excludes establishing residence, and working on it is irregular. Action: do not onboard or payroll anyone until the M-Trabajador visa is granted.

entity_title: Apply for the visa online, not at a consulate
fact_text: Colombian visas are applied for through an electronic form on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería) website; the application can be filed from abroad or from within Colombia. There is no requirement to lodge the M-Trabajador application in person at a consulate.
evidence_quote: Diligenciar formulario de solicitud de visa de forma electrónica disponible en la página de internet de la entidad

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the work visa must be obtained at a Colombian consulate before travel. Actually it is filed online via the Cancillería portal and can be requested while the applicant is already in Colombia on a regular entry. Action: prepare the digital dossier (photo under 300kb, passport valid 6+ months, employer documents) for the online form.

fact_text: A foreigner becomes a Colombian tax resident once present in the country for more than 183 calendar days (counting entry and exit days) within any 365-day period. If the 183 days straddle two tax years, residency starts in the second year.
evidence_quote: Permanecer continúa o discontinuamente en el país por más 183 días calendario incluyendo días de entrada y salida del país, durante un periodo cualquiera de 365 días calendario consecutivos

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed tax residency follows the visa type or the calendar year. Actually it is a rolling day-count test (>183 days in any 365-day window), independent of visa. Action: track the assignee's days in Colombia from day one.

entity_title: Budget for tax on worldwide income once resident
fact_text: Once resident for tax purposes, a foreigner is taxed by Colombia (DIAN) on income and capital gains from both Colombian and foreign sources, and on assets held inside and outside the country. Since Ley 1607 of 2012 this applies from the first year of residency, with no grace period for foreigners.
evidence_quote: Las personas naturales, nacionales o extranjeras, residentes en el país y las sucesiones ilíquidas de causantes con residencia en el país en el momento de su muerte, están sujetas al impuesto sobre la renta y complementarios en lo concerniente a sus rentas y ganancias ocasionales, tanto de fuente nacional como de fuente extranjera, y a su patrimonio poseído dentro y fuera del país.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a foreigner is taxed only on their Colombian salary. Actually a tax resident is taxed on worldwide income and global assets from the first year of residency (the old 5-year grace was repealed by Ley 1607/2012). Action: model global tax exposure and any double-tax-treaty relief before the assignee passes 183 days.

entity_title: Register a RUT tax number, separate from the ID
fact_text: To be an income-tax filer in Colombia the foreign employee must register in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) administered by DIAN, which assigns the NIT tax number. The RUT is the single mechanism DIAN uses to identify taxpayers and is distinct from the cédula de extranjería.
evidence_quote: El Registro Único Tributario, RUT, administrado por la Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales, constituye el mecanismo único para identificar, ubicar y clasificar las personas y entidades que tengan la calidad de contribuyentes declarantes del impuesto sobre la renta

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the cédula de extranjería doubles as the tax ID. Actually income-tax filers need a separate RUT registration, which yields the NIT. Action: register the employee in the RUT once they hold a cédula and before they must file or transact with DIAN.

entity_title: Enrol every employee in a health EPS
fact_text: Anyone on a Colombian employment contract, including a foreign worker, must be affiliated to the contributory health regime (EPS) under Ley 100. Unlike pensions, there is no home-country-coverage exemption for health, so both employee and employer must contribute to a Colombian EPS.
evidence_quote: Los afiliados al Sistema mediante el régimen contributivo son las personas vinculadas a través de contrato de trabajo, los servidores públicos, los pensionados y jubilados y los trabajadores independientes con capacidad de pago.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a global or private health policy lets a foreigner skip local health enrolment. Actually contributory-regime (EPS) affiliation is mandatory for everyone with an employment contract, with no foreign-coverage exemption. Action: enrol the employee in an EPS as part of payroll onboarding.

entity_title: Check whether the pension is optional for the assignee
fact_text: Ley 100 lists foreigners who work in Colombia under an employment contract but are not covered by a pension scheme in their home country (or any other) as voluntary, not compulsory, members of the pension system. In practice an assignee who keeps home-country pension coverage can generally opt out of the Colombian pension contribution, though health (EPS) affiliation still applies.
evidence_quote: Los extranjeros que en virtud de un contrato de trabajo permanezcan en el país y no estén cubiertos por algún régimen de su país de origen o de cualquier otro.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a foreign employee must pay into the Colombian pension like a local. Actually the law treats foreign workers on a contract as voluntary pension affiliates, and one already covered by a home-country scheme can generally opt out. Action: document the assignee's foreign pension coverage to justify the exemption and confirm health/EPS is still paid.

entity_title: Re-apply before any change of role or employer
fact_text: The M-Trabajador visa authorises work only for the specific role, employer, profession or activity it was granted for. A change of employer, position or type of work invalidates the permit and requires a new visa application, and such changes must also be reported to the Cancillería by the employer.
evidence_quote: Esta visa otorga permiso de trabajo exclusivamente para el cargo, entidad, profesión o actividad para la cual se otorgó.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work visa lets the holder take any job or move within the group. Actually the M-Trabajador permit is locked to the exact role and employer named in the application. Action: apply for a new visa before any change of employer, position or duties.

entity_title: Watch long absences that void the M visa
fact_text: A Migrant (M) visa is automatically cancelled if the holder is absent from Colombia for more than 180 continuous calendar days within any 365-day period counted from the visa's issue date. This is a real risk for a globally mobile executive who spends long stretches outside the country.
evidence_quote: Las visas de Migrante (M) cuyos titulares se ausenten del país por más de ciento ochenta (180) días calendario continuos, dentro de cada trescientos sesenta y cinco (365) días contados a partir de la expedición de su visa, perderán automáticamente su vigencia.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a valid multi-year M visa stays valid regardless of travel. Actually it lapses automatically after 180 continuous days abroad in any 365-day window. Action: monitor the assignee's continuous time outside Colombia and plan re-entries to preserve the visa.

entity_title: Plan a five-year horizon for permanent residence
fact_text: Time held on an M-Trabajador visa counts toward the permanent Resident (R) visa por tiempo acumulado, but the qualifying period for the worker category is five years of continuous M-visa holding under Article 90, longer than the two to three years some family-based M categories require.
evidence_quote: Esta visa permite acumular tiempo para la Visa de Residente en los términos del Artículo 90 de la presente Resolución.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a couple of years on any Colombian visa leads to permanent residence. Actually the M-Trabajador category needs five years of continuous M-visa holding to qualify for the R visa by accumulated time. Action: set a five-year expectation for work-based permanent residence and keep every prior visa and migration record for the R application.
